source_refs.note: Book p. 50-51: 4.2.4 Multiplication of two Matrices: conformability, the 2x3 by 3x2 product with Figure (A), AB (i) and BA (ii), Note 1, Note 2 with its order diagram, Example 2 (A^2 B) and the Note on powers of square matrices. Teaching notes, our worked illustration, the extra steps of the...

blocks.text: Ab is unit ka sab se aham operation: do matrices ki zarb (multiplication). Yeh addition jaisa khana ba khana nahin hota; is ka apna "row guna column" wala tareeqa hai. Aaj ke baad aap determinant, inverse aur equations ke hal, sab mein yahi tareeqa istemal karenge, is liye ise itminan se samjhiye.
Kitab ki pehli shart: do matrices \(A\) aur \(B\) product \(AB\) ke liye conformable kehlati hain agar \(A\) ke columns ki tadaad \(B\) ki rows ki tadaad ke barabar ho.

Ab definition: maan lijiye \(A = [a_{ij}]\) ek \(2 \times 3\) matrix hai aur \(B = [b_{ij}]\) ek \(3 \times 2\) matrix. To product \(AB\) woh \(2 \times 2\) matrix \(C\) hai jis ka element \(c_{ij}\) \(A\) ki \(i\)th row ke elements aur \(B\) ke \(j\)th column ke corresponding elements ke products ka jama hai. Misaal ke tor par \(C\) ka element \(c_{21}\) figure (A) mein dikhaya gaya hai, yani

blocks.alt: Labelled 2nd row of A: the entries a21, a22, a23 across the bottom. Bent arrows (magenta, cyan, magenta) go up from a21, a22 and a23 and across to b11, b21 and b31, written one below the other on the right under the heading 1st column of B.
blocks.caption: Figure (A): the 2nd row of A meets the 1st column of B to give c21 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
\[c_{21} = a_{21}b_{11} + a_{22}b_{21} + a_{23}b_{31}\]
Figure ko yun parhiye: \(A\) ki doosri row ki pehli entry \(B\) ke pehle column ki pehli entry se, doosri entry doosri se, teesri entry teesri se zarb hoti hai, aur teeno products jama ho kar \(c_{21}\) bante hain. "2" isliye ke row 2 li, "1" isliye ke column 1 liya. Is tarah

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Row guna column hi kyun? \(A\) ki har row mein 3 entries hain aur \(B\) ke har column mein bhi 3. Is liye inhein jori jori milaya ja sakta hai: pehli ke saath pehli, doosri ke saath doosri, teesri ke saath teesri. Har jori ko zarb do aur jama kar lo. Isi wajah se shart hai ke \(A\) ke columns = \(B\) ki rows; warna koi entry bina saathi ke reh jayegi.
Tareeqa: \(c_{ij}\) nikalne ke liye baayen haath ki ungli \(A\) ki row \(i\) par rakhiye aur daayen haath ki ungli \(B\) ke column \(j\) par; dono ko saath saath chalaiye, ek aari, ek khari.
(Kitab ke scan mein figure (A) ke labels saaf nahin parhe jate; sahi joriyan yeh hain: \(a_{21}\) ke saath \(b_{11}\), \(a_{22}\) ke saath \(b_{21}\), \(a_{23}\) ke saath \(b_{31}\).)
Isi tarah

Ghor kijiye: yahan \(B\) ki har row mein 2 entries hain aur \(A\) ke har column mein bhi 2, is liye har entry mein do products jama hote hain. (i) aur (ii) se, \(AB\) aur \(BA\) dono nikal aaye, lekin un ke orders bil-tarteeb \(2 \times 2\) aur \(3 \times 3\) hain. Yani yeh do bilkul alag matrices hain; barabar ho hi nahin saktin.

blocks.title: Note 1
blocks.text: Aam tor par \(AB \ne BA\).

Note 1 ki teen soorat-e-haal samajh lijiye. (1) Kabhi \(AB\) define hota hai magar \(BA\) nahin: jaise \(A\) \(2 \times 3\) aur \(B\) \(3 \times 4\) ho to \(AB\) \(2 \times 4\) banta hai, lekin \(BA\) ke liye \((3 \times 4)(2 \times 3)\) mein andar wale 4 aur 2 barabar nahin. (2) Kabhi dono define hote hain magar orders alag hote hain, jaise upar \(2 \times 2\) aur \(3 \times 3\). (3) Kabhi dono same order ke hote hain phir bhi entries alag hoti hain, jaise neeche hamari misaal mein. Bohat kam aisa hota hai ke \(AB\) aur \(BA\) bilkul barabar niklein.

blocks.title: Note 2
blocks.text: Agar product \(AB\) define ho, to us ka order yun samjha ja sakta hai: \(A\) ka order \(m \times n\), \(B\) ka order \(n \times p\), aur \(AB\) ka order \(m \times p\).

blocks.alt: Three lines: Order of A, m × n; Order of B, n × p; Order of AB, m × p, each order in a pale blue box. A curved arrow on the left goes from m in the order of A to m in the order of AB; a curved arrow on the right goes from p in the order of B to p in the order of AB.
blocks.caption: Figure: Note 2, the order of the product AB (original drawing after the textbook's diagram)

blocks.text: Note 2 ko yaad karne ka aasan tareeqa: dono orders saath likhiye, \((m \times n)(n \times p)\). Andar wale do number (\(n\) aur \(n\)) barabar hon to product mumkin hai, aur bahar wale do number (\(m\) aur \(p\)) jawab ka order bata dete hain. Jaise \((2 \times 3)(3 \times 2) = 2 \times 2\) aur \((3 \times 2)(2 \times 3) = 3 \times 3\); yahi upar (i) aur (ii) mein hua.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin. \(C = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) aur \(D = \begin{bmatrix}5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8\end{bmatrix}\). Orders \((2 \times 2)(2 \times 2)\), andar wale 2 barabar, jawab \(2 \times 2\).
\[c_{11} = (1)(5) + (2)(7) = 19\]
\[c_{12} = (1)(6) + (2)(8) = 22\]
\[c_{21} = (3)(5) + (4)(7) = 43\]
\[c_{22} = (3)(6) + (4)(8) = 50\]
\[CD = \begin{bmatrix}19 & 22 \\ 43 & 50\end{bmatrix}\]
Ab ulti tarteeb mein:
\[DC = \begin{bmatrix}23 & 34 \\ 31 & 46\end{bmatrix}\]
Dono products mojood hain, phir bhi \(CD \ne DC\). Yahi Note 1 hai: matrices mein factors ki tarteeb badalne se jawab badal jata hai, numbers ki tarah nahin (\(3 \times 5 = 5 \times 3\)).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}\) ka order kya hoga, aur jawab?
Jawab: \((1 \times 3)(3 \times 1) = 1 \times 1\), yani ek hi entry: \(1(4) + 2(5) + 3(6) = 32\), to jawab \([32]\). Aur ulti tarteeb \((3 \times 1)(1 \times 3)\) ka order \(3 \times 3\) hoga! Dekha, tarteeb badli to shakal hi badal gayi.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(A\) ka order \(2 \times 3\) aur \(B\) ka order \(2 \times 3\) ho to kya \(AB\) mumkin hai? Aur \(AB^{t}\)?
Jawab: \(AB\) nahin, kyun ke \((2 \times 3)(2 \times 3)\) mein andar wale 3 aur 2 barabar nahin. Lekin \(B^{t}\) ka order \(3 \times 2\) hai, is liye \(AB^{t}\) ka order \((2 \times 3)(3 \times 2) = 2 \times 2\) hai, yani mumkin hai. Transpose kabhi kabhi na-mumkin product ko mumkin bana deta hai.

Ab kitab ka Example 2. Is mein do products ek ke baad ek nikalne hain, is liye pehle plan bana lete hain. \(A^{2}B\) ka matlab hai \(A \cdot A \cdot B\). Associative property (4.3) ki wajah se hum pehle \(A \cdot A\) nikal kar phir \(B\) se zarb de sakte hain; kitab yahi karti hai. Har \(3 \times 3\) product mein nau entries hain aur har entry mein teen products ka jama hai, yani kaafi hisaab hai. Is liye hum har row alag step mein karenge aur har entry poori likhenge, taa ke aap har number ka hisaab khud check kar sakein.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps:
Given: \(A\) aur \(B\), dono \(3 \times 3\).
To find: \(A^{2}B\).
Method: \(A^{2}\) ka matlab \(A \cdot A\) hai (har entry ka square nahin!). Pehle \(A^{2} = A \cdot A\) nikalenge, phir us ko \(B\) se multiply karenge. Har entry row guna column ke qaide se aayegi. Orders: \(3 \times 3\) guna \(3 \times 3\), andar wale 3 barabar, is liye har product mumkin hai aur jawab bhi \(3 \times 3\) hoga.

Step 1: \(A^{2} = A \cdot A\) ki pehli row (\(p_{ij}\) = \(A^{2}\) ki entries)
\[p_{11} = (2)(2) + (-1)(1) + (0)(1) = 3\]
\[p_{12} = (2)(-1) + (-1)(2) + (0)(2) = -4\]
\[p_{13} = (2)(0) + (-1)(-3) + (0)(-2) = 3\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki row 1 ko \(A\) ke har column se milaya: pehli entry pehli se, doosri doosri se, teesri teesri se zarb, phir teeno ka jama. Yaad rakhiye ke yahan \(A\) do martaba aa raha hai: baayen wali \(A\) se row li jati hai aur daayen wali \(A\) se column. Ek row se teen entries banti hain, kyun ke columns teen hain.

Step 2: \(A^{2} = A \cdot A\) ki doosri row (\(p_{ij}\) = \(A^{2}\) ki entries)
\[p_{21} = (1)(2) + (2)(1) + (-3)(1) = 1\]
\[p_{22} = (1)(-1) + (2)(2) + (-3)(2) = -3\]
\[p_{23} = (1)(0) + (2)(-3) + (-3)(-2) = 0\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki row 2 ko \(A\) ke har column se milaya: pehli entry pehli se, doosri doosri se, teesri teesri se zarb, phir teeno ka jama. Yaad rakhiye ke yahan \(A\) do martaba aa raha hai: baayen wali \(A\) se row li jati hai aur daayen wali \(A\) se column. Ek row se teen entries banti hain, kyun ke columns teen hain.

Step 3: \(A^{2} = A \cdot A\) ki teesri row (\(p_{ij}\) = \(A^{2}\) ki entries)
\[p_{31} = (1)(2) + (2)(1) + (-2)(1) = 2\]
\[p_{32} = (1)(-1) + (2)(2) + (-2)(2) = -1\]
\[p_{33} = (1)(0) + (2)(-3) + (-2)(-2) = -2\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki row 3 ko \(A\) ke har column se milaya: pehli entry pehli se, doosri doosri se, teesri teesri se zarb, phir teeno ka jama. Yaad rakhiye ke yahan \(A\) do martaba aa raha hai: baayen wali \(A\) se row li jati hai aur daayen wali \(A\) se column. Ek row se teen entries banti hain, kyun ke columns teen hain.

Step 4: \(A^{2}\) likhein
\[A^{2} = \begin{bmatrix}3 & -4 & 3 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & -2\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: upar ki nau entries apni apni jagah par rakhi hain.

Step 5: \(A^{2}B\) ki pehli row (\(q_{ij}\) = \(A^{2}B\) ki entries)
\[q_{11} = (3)(2) + (-4)(-1) + (3)(0) = 10\]
\[q_{12} = (3)(-2) + (-4)(-4) + (3)(-5) = -5\]
\[q_{13} = (3)(3) + (-4)(6) + (3)(5) = 0\]
Kyun: ab \(A^{2}\) ki row 1 ko \(B\) ke har column se milaya. Negative numbers bracket mein hain taa ke sign ki ghalti na ho. Dhyan dein: minus guna minus plus hota hai, jaise \((-4)(-4) = 16\), aur minus guna plus minus, jaise \((3)(-5) = -15\). Pehle teeno products alag alag likhiye, phir jama kijiye; zehan mein ek saath sab karne se ghalti hoti hai.

Step 6: \(A^{2}B\) ki doosri row (\(q_{ij}\) = \(A^{2}B\) ki entries)
\[q_{21} = (1)(2) + (-3)(-1) + (0)(0) = 5\]
\[q_{22} = (1)(-2) + (-3)(-4) + (0)(-5) = 10\]
\[q_{23} = (1)(3) + (-3)(6) + (0)(5) = -15\]
Kyun: ab \(A^{2}\) ki row 2 ko \(B\) ke har column se milaya. Negative numbers bracket mein hain taa ke sign ki ghalti na ho. Dhyan dein: minus guna minus plus hota hai, jaise \((-4)(-4) = 16\), aur minus guna plus minus, jaise \((3)(-5) = -15\). Pehle teeno products alag alag likhiye, phir jama kijiye; zehan mein ek saath sab karne se ghalti hoti hai.

Step 7: \(A^{2}B\) ki teesri row (\(q_{ij}\) = \(A^{2}B\) ki entries)
\[q_{31} = (2)(2) + (-1)(-1) + (-2)(0) = 5\]
\[q_{32} = (2)(-2) + (-1)(-4) + (-2)(-5) = 10\]
\[q_{33} = (2)(3) + (-1)(6) + (-2)(5) = -10\]
Kyun: ab \(A^{2}\) ki row 3 ko \(B\) ke har column se milaya. Negative numbers bracket mein hain taa ke sign ki ghalti na ho. Dhyan dein: minus guna minus plus hota hai, jaise \((-4)(-4) = 16\), aur minus guna plus minus, jaise \((3)(-5) = -15\). Pehle teeno products alag alag likhiye, phir jama kijiye; zehan mein ek saath sab karne se ghalti hoti hai.

Tasdeeq: ek doosre raaste se ek entry dekhiye. \(A^{2}B = A(AB)\) bhi hai (associative property, 4.3). \(AB\) ka pehla column: \(2(2) + (-1)(-1) + 0(0) = 5\), \(1(2) + 2(-1) + (-3)(0) = 0\), \(1(2) + 2(-1) + (-2)(0) = 0\). Phir \(A\) ki pehli row guna yeh column: \(2(5) + (-1)(0) + 0(0) = 10\), jo \(q_{11} = 10\) se milta hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Square matrices ki powers yun define hoti hain: \(A^{2} = A \times A\), \(A^{3} = A \times A \times A\), \(A^{n} = A \times A \times A \times \cdots\) \(n\) factors tak.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Powers sirf square matrices ki hoti hain: \(A \cdot A\) tabhi define hai jab \(A\) ke columns aur \(A\) ki rows barabar hon, yani \(A\) square ho.
Dhyan dein: \(A^{2}\) kabhi bhi har entry ka square le kar nahin banta. \(C = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) ke liye \(C^{2} = \begin{bmatrix}7 & 10 \\ 15 & 22\end{bmatrix}\), na ke \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ 9 & 16 \end{bmatrix}\). Misaal: row 1, column 1 = \(1(1) + 2(3) = 7\).
\(A^{3}\) nikalna ho to pehle \(A^{2}\) nikaliye, phir use \(A\) se zarb dijiye: \(A^{3} = A^{2} \cdot A\). Isi tarah har agli power pichli power ko \(A\) se zarb dene se milti hai, is liye hisaab ko qadam ba qadam rakhiye aur har qadam ka jawab likh kar aage barhiye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(AB\) sirf tab define hai jab (\(A\) ke columns) = (\(B\) ki rows).
2. \(c_{ij}\) = \(A\) ki row \(i\) guna \(B\) ka column \(j\): joriyan zarb karo, phir jama.
3. Order ka qaida: \((m \times n)(n \times p) = m \times p\); andar wale barabar, bahar wale jawab.
4. Aam tor par \(AB \ne BA\); kabhi to ek define hi nahin hota.
5. \(A^{n} = A \cdot A \cdots A\) (\(n\) factors), sirf square \(A\) ke liye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Addition ki tarah khana ba khana zarb (\(a_{ij}b_{ij}\)) kar dena. Matrix multiplication row guna column hai.
2. \(A\) ka column ya \(B\) ki row utha lena. Yaad rakhiye: pehli matrix se aari row, doosri se khara column.
3. \(AB = BA\) samajh kar factors ki tarteeb badal dena.
4. \(A^{2}\) ko entries ke squares likh dena.
5. Negative entries mein sign ki ghalti: unhein bracket mein rakhiye, \((-1)(-4) = 4\).
